simple.meaning: מַעְגָּל (maʻgâl) appears 16 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with flocks.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, beginning at 1 Samuel 17:20. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, righteousness, land, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעְגָּל (H4570) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows מַעְגָּל through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: מַעְגָּל (maʻgâl) / H4570 is tracked through 1 Samuel 17:20, 1 Samuel 26:5, 1 Samuel 26:7, Psalms 17:5. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the place of the wagons, as the army which was going out to the fight shouted for the battle.

timeline.evidenceText: David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the place of the wagons, as the army which was going out to the fight shouted for the battle.

Then David arose, and came to the place where Saul had encamped; and David saw the place where Saul lay, with Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his army. Saul lay within the place of the wagons, and the people were encamped around him.

So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the place of the wagons, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay around him.
My steps have held fast to your paths.
I said to Yahweh, “You are my God.”
Then you will understand righteousness and justice,
who are crooked in their ways,
for her house leads down to death,
I have taught you in the way of wisdom.
Make the path of your feet level.
She gives no thought to the way of life.
For the ways of man are before Yahweh’s eyes.
The way of the just is uprightness.
They don’t know the way of peace;

definitions.full: H4570. magal or magalah מַעְגָּל noun masculine Psa 65:12 1 entrenchment ; 2 track ; — absolute ׳מ 1Sam 26:5 +, with ה locative הַמַּעְגָּ֫לָה 17:20 ; construct מַעְגַּל Proverbs 5:26 +; plural construct מַעְגְּלֵי Psa 23:3 ; Prov 4:11 ; suffix מַעְגָּלֶיךָ Psa 65:12 , elsewhere מַעְגְּלוֺתֶיךָ 17:5 , מַעְגְּלֹתָיו Prov 5:21 , תֶיהָ - 2:12 ; 5:6 , תָם - 2:15 ; Isa 59:8 ; — 1 circumvallation, entrenchment 1Sam 17:20 ; 26:5 , 7 . 2 track (properly wagon-track ), only figurative: a. in figurative of snares of wicked Psa 140:6 . b. = course of action, or life, ׳מ רַגֱל֑ךָ Prov 4:26 , ׳מ 5:21 (|| דַּרְכֵיאִֿישׁ ); specifically good, right, ׳מ צֶדֶק Psa 23:3 , ׳מ ישֶׁר Prov 4:11 , ׳מ טוֺב 2:9 , ׳מ צַדִּיק Isa 26:7 ; bad sense Prov 2:15 , 18 ; 5:6 ; Isa 59:8 ; tracks of ׳י are those approved by him Psa 17:5 ; or those traversed by him, דָּ֑שֶׁן וִרְעֲפוּן מַעְגָּלֶיךָ 65:12 figurative of richly-laden cart dropping its contents in its track.
definitions.rootNote: or feminine מַעְגָּלָה ; from the same as 5696 ;
